title: Horse Chestnut: Ancient Conker Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Every conker in Europe descends from a few ravines in Greece and Albania, where the species is now vulnerable. Seventeen old chestnuts, fifteen cities.
intro: Every conker in Europe descends from a handful of mountain ravines in northern Greece, Albania and North Macedonia, the only places the horse chestnut still grows wild and where it is now classed as vulnerable. Everywhere else it is a planted tree, and cities planted it hard. Vienna lined its grandest avenue with chestnuts from 1840. Munich's brewers put them over their beer cellars, because the species throws heavy shade from shallow roots that will not force their way into a vault, and the beer garden followed from there. Geneva went further than anyone: since 1818 an official has walked to a designated chestnut each spring, recorded the date its first leaf opens and reported it to the press, which makes one of the longest continuous records of its kind anywhere. Seventeen are mapped, in fifteen cities, and not one of them is anywhere near the wild population.
